# Tech Destination Sri Lanka

> Tech Destination Sri Lanka helps companies abroad hire technology talent, find software outsourcing partners and set up teams in Sri Lanka. It publishes sourced reporting on the software, products and companies built by Sri Lankan technology talent. Through Source from Sri Lanka it also connects buyers abroad with Sri Lankan exporters of tea, cinnamon, coconut products, apparel, rubber products, electrical equipment and more, and runs Tender Radar, international tender alerts and bid support for Sri Lankan exporters.

Sri Lanka is UTC+5:30. Colombo is the main technology hub. Every story lists its sources at the end.

## Key facts
- How big are Sri Lanka's IT and BPM exports? USD 1.645 billion in 2025, up 8.8% on the year, according to the Export Development Board. The Central Bank's narrower balance of payments measure records about USD 0.8 billion, and the industry estimates about USD 2 billion, because revenue booked abroad and freelance income are not fully captured.
- How many people work in tech in Sri Lanka? The Export Development Board cites 146,000 people employed in the sector. Press reports of industry estimates in 2026 put it at about 175,000. The last full official survey counted 124,873 ICT workers in 2018.
- How many ICT graduates does Sri Lanka produce each year? Startup Genome's 2026 report says 12,000+. Industry estimates reported in the press in 2026 say about 17,000 enter the sector each year.
- How does Sri Lanka rank for tech talent? Third in Asia for affordable tech talent in Startup Genome's Global Startup Ecosystem Report 2026, which also recorded Sri Lanka climbing more than 65 places in its emerging ecosystem rankings, the biggest jump that year.
- What are the biggest Sri Lankan tech exits? Virtusa, cofounded by a Sri Lankan, was acquired for USD 2 billion in 2021. WSO2 was acquired by EQT for USD 600 million in 2024. The London Stock Exchange bought MillenniumIT after choosing its trading platform. JPMorganChase acquired WealthOS in 2026.
- Which global companies run R&D in Sri Lanka? IFS does about 60% of its global product development in Colombo. Sysco, Synopsys and Zebra Technologies run engineering or R&D centres there. HCLTech, EY, HSBC and WNS run delivery operations.
- Who are the largest tech employers in Sri Lanka? Virtusa has 3,000+ engineers in Colombo and IFS has 2,200+ employees there.
- What time zone is Sri Lanka in? UTC+5:30 all year, with no daylight saving. That is 1.5 hours ahead of the UAE, 3.5 to 4.5 hours ahead of Central Europe, 4.5 to 5.5 hours ahead of the UK and 9.5 to 10.5 hours ahead of US Eastern time.
- What does a software engineer earn in Sri Lanka? A median of about LKR 177,000 a month (about USD 535) according to self reported Glassdoor data for 2026, and about LKR 260,000 for a senior engineer. Export focused employers pay more.
- What tax do IT exporters pay in Sri Lanka? 15% on income from services exported and paid for in foreign currency, from 1 April 2025. The standard corporate rate is 30%.
- Can foreigners fully own a tech company in Sri Lanka? Yes. IT and software companies can be 100% foreign owned and can repatriate profits, according to the Board of Investment.
- Which universities feed the tech industry? The University of Moratuwa, a top contributor to Google Summer of Code since 2004, and SLIIT, the largest private tech university with 25,000+ students, are the best known. Peradeniya and Ruhuna teach chip design with a curriculum built with Synopsys.
- Where are the main tech parks in Colombo? Orion City in Colombo 09 houses 85+ technology companies. TRACE Expert City in Colombo 10, the World Trade Center in Colombo 01 and Port City Colombo are the other main hubs.
- Is there an AI industry in Sri Lanka? Yes. Roar Global runs the country's first AI gateway, Xeynergy builds its own AI products and Rootcode builds AI platforms for the Estonian government.

## Outsourcing business services to Sri Lanka
- [Accounting and bookkeeping outsourcing to Sri Lanka](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/offshoring/accounting-bookkeeping-outsourcing-sri-lanka/): Sri Lanka has one of the deepest pools of professionally qualified accountants of any offshore destination: CA Sri Lanka alone has more than 9,000 members and 40,000 students, and around 15,000 people are CIMA students or members. Global banks and exchanges run finance operations in Colombo, including HSBC since 2004 and the London Stock Exchange Group, whose Colombo hubs employ more than 1,600 people. Accounting firms and companies in the UK, Australia, the US and the Gulf outsource bookkeeping, accounts payable and receivable, reconciliations, month-end close and management reporting to Sri Lankan teams.
- [Investment research and KPO outsourcing to Sri Lanka](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/offshoring/investment-research-kpo-sri-lanka/): Colombo has supported Wall Street and City of London firms for more than two decades. Amba Research, now part of Acuity Knowledge Partners, started in Sri Lanka in 2003, and Acuity's Colombo team serves more than 50 global financial institutions with equity and fixed income research, credit analytics, quantitative work and investment banking support. The London Stock Exchange Group employs more than 1,600 people in Colombo, including data and analytics roles.
- [Hire virtual assistants and remote admin staff in Sri Lanka](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/offshoring/virtual-assistants-sri-lanka/): Australian, UK and Gulf businesses hire virtual and executive assistants in Sri Lanka through remote staffing firms that employ the assistant locally and manage payroll, equipment and compliance. The strongest demand comes from Australia, where the time zone gives a shared afternoon, and from the UAE, which works almost the same day. The role is changing fast: routine scheduling and inbox work is being handled by AI, so the best Sri Lankan assistants are hired as operations coordinators who run those tools and own workflows.
- [Digital marketing outsourcing to Sri Lanka](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/offshoring/digital-marketing-outsourcing-sri-lanka/): Sri Lankan agencies and remote teams run SEO, paid search and social, content, email and marketing operations for clients in Australia, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and the UK. Digital marketing, advertising and PR outsourcing is one of the business services the Export Development Board promotes, and Australian firms are now building dedicated offshore marketing teams in Colombo. Evidence on the size of this market is thin, so judge providers on case studies rather than country statistics.
- [Customer support and back office outsourcing to Sri Lanka](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/offshoring/customer-support-outsourcing-sri-lanka/): Sri Lanka's strongest track record in customer operations is in banking, insurance and complex servicing rather than high volume call centres. HSBC has served customers in 24 markets from Colombo since 2004, a global business process firm that has delivered from Colombo for more than 20 years added over 300 jobs in 2025, and local business process firms run contact centres for airlines, hospitality and retail. The time zone suits UK, Gulf and Australian customers well. For live US hours, teams work night shifts.
- [Medical billing and revenue cycle outsourcing to Sri Lanka](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/offshoring/medical-billing-outsourcing-sri-lanka/): Sri Lanka has a long running healthcare revenue cycle industry serving mainly US hospitals and practices. Medical billing, coding, claims submission, payment posting, denials management and AR follow-up are delivered from Colombo and Kandy, where one provider opened a 300 seat centre in 2024. The overnight time difference with the US means claims worked in Sri Lanka are processed by the time US offices open.
- [Legal process outsourcing (LPO) to Sri Lanka](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/offshoring/legal-process-outsourcing-sri-lanka/): Sri Lankan legal process outsourcing firms provide paralegal support, contract drafting and review, legal research, matter administration and company secretarial work for law firms and in-house teams in the UK, Australia, Singapore and the US. Sri Lankan lawyers train in English in a system with common law roots, which makes them a natural fit for UK and Australian work. This is a small, specialist market: choose providers on the jurisdictions they already serve.
- [Engineering design, BIM and quantity surveying outsourcing to Sri Lanka](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/offshoring/engineering-design-bim-outsourcing-sri-lanka/): Sri Lankan engineering and design firms deliver BIM modelling, Revit and CAD drafting, structural detailing, 3D visualisation and quantity surveying for construction clients in the UK, Australia and the Gulf. Quantity surveying is a well established profession in Sri Lanka with strong links to Gulf construction, and university research identifies BIM modelling and bill of quantities preparation as well suited to outsourcing. This is a growing, specialist area with smaller firms rather than large centres.
- [Data annotation and AI training data services in Sri Lanka](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/offshoring/data-annotation-sri-lanka/): Sri Lankan companies provide data annotation, image labelling, data conversion and content processing for international clients, and some have done data work for more than 30 years. It is an emerging rather than a large scale capability: there is no big dedicated annotation centre, but there are established data processing firms and a growing pool of graduates for higher value work such as LLM evaluation and Sinhala and Tamil language data.
- [Insurance back office, HR and payroll outsourcing to Sri Lanka](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/offshoring/insurance-hr-payroll-outsourcing-sri-lanka/): UK insurers and global software groups run back office operations from Colombo. In October 2025 the UK specialist insurer CFC opened a 200 seat global services hub in Colombo, and a company owned by private equity investors hired 370 people in nine months to serve portfolio companies in the Americas and Europe, including business process work. Sri Lankan firms also run payroll, HR and recruitment process outsourcing for Australian and UK employers.
- [Outsourcing to Sri Lanka from the UK](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/offshoring/from-uk/): UK businesses have outsourced to Sri Lanka for more than 20 years. HSBC opened its Colombo operations in 2004, the London Stock Exchange Group employs more than 1,600 people there, and in 2025 the UK specialist insurer CFC opened a 200 seat hub in Colombo. Sri Lanka is 4.5 hours ahead of the UK in summer and 5.5 in winter, so a team starting early afternoon covers the full UK day, and work processed in the Sri Lankan morning is ready before London opens.
- [Outsourcing to Sri Lanka from Australia](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/offshoring/from-australia/): Australian businesses are one of Sri Lanka's main outsourcing markets, especially accounting firms, professional services and growing companies hiring offshore staff. Sri Lanka is 4.5 to 5.5 hours behind Sydney and 2.5 hours behind Perth, so the Sri Lankan morning overlaps the Australian afternoon and overnight work is ready for the next morning. Remote staffing providers in Colombo employ staff locally for Australian clients, and Australian firms signed new contracts to build Sri Lankan teams in 2026.
- [Outsourcing to Sri Lanka from the USA](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/offshoring/from-usa/): US companies use Sri Lanka mainly for work that benefits from an overnight turnaround: medical billing and revenue cycle management, investment research, finance operations and data work. Sri Lanka is 9.5 to 13.5 hours ahead of the US, so claims, reconciliations and research processed during the Sri Lankan day are ready when US offices open. Investment research firms in Colombo serve Wall Street institutions, and revenue cycle firms serve US hospitals and practices.
- [Outsourcing to Sri Lanka from the UAE and the Gulf](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/offshoring/from-uae/): For companies in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and the wider Gulf, Sri Lanka is one of the closest offshore options: 1.5 hours ahead of the UAE and a short flight from Colombo. Sri Lankan teams already work in Gulf construction, finance and hospitality, and providers serve UAE clients with accountants, quantity surveyors, marketers, support agents and virtual assistants who share almost the whole working day.
- [BPO and outsourcing companies in Sri Lanka](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/offshoring/bpo-companies-sri-lanka/): Organisations delivering business services from Sri Lanka, by service, with sources

## Sri Lanka compared with other offshore destinations
- [Sri Lanka vs Vietnam](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/compare/vietnam/): Vietnam is the bigger market, with about 530,000 programmers and a top ten place in Kearney's 2023 services location index. Sri Lanka is smaller, with about 175,000 IT and business process professionals, but has a longer record of core product R&D for Western software companies: IFS, Sysco, Synopsys and the London Stock Exchange Group all build there. Choose Vietnam for scale and hardware adjacent work. Choose Sri Lanka for long running product teams, enterprise software and business in English.
- [Sri Lanka vs The Philippines](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/compare/philippines/): The Philippines is far larger in business process outsourcing, with 1.9 million workers and the best English score in Asia on the EF index. Most of that workforce is contact centre and back office. Sri Lanka is a smaller market weighted toward software engineering, product R&D and qualified finance work. Choose the Philippines for customer support and voice at scale. Choose Sri Lanka for software engineering, ERP and accounting.
- [Sri Lanka vs Poland](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/compare/poland/): Poland is Europe's largest nearshore engineering market, inside the EU, with very high English and Google's biggest EU engineering hub. It costs roughly twice as much as Sri Lanka: senior rates of USD 45 to 60 an hour against about USD 25 to 40. Choose Poland when you need EU jurisdiction, the same time zone and short flights. Choose Sri Lanka when budget matters and four to five hours of daily overlap is enough.
- [Sri Lanka vs Ukraine](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/compare/ukraine/): Ukraine has a deep engineering culture and exported USD 6.45 billion of IT services in 2024, about four times Sri Lanka's total. The war is the deciding factor: 75% of Ukrainian IT companies have mobilised employees and most new sites opened in 2025 were abroad. Many buyers now add a second location. Sri Lanka offers lower rates and no conflict risk, at the cost of a wider time difference from Europe.
- [Sri Lanka vs Romania](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/compare/romania/): Romania combines EU membership with the best English score of any major outsourcing country, 11th in the world. Its IT workforce is about the size of Sri Lanka's and costs more: senior rates of USD 40 to 55 an hour against about USD 25 to 40. Romania removed its income tax exemption for IT workers in 2025. Choose Romania for EU jurisdiction and time zone. Choose Sri Lanka for cost and for enterprise software depth.
- [Sri Lanka vs Latin America](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/compare/latin-america/): For US companies, Mexico and Colombia offer something Sri Lanka cannot: the same working day. They cost more, with senior rates of USD 40 to 55 an hour and regional averages up to USD 75, against about USD 25 to 40 for Sri Lanka. National English scores are lower in Mexico and similar in Colombia. Choose Latin America when real time collaboration all day is essential. Choose Sri Lanka when a shifted schedule or overnight progress works and cost matters.

## Sri Lanka export facts
- What are Sri Lanka's main exports? Apparel and textiles (US$4.91 billion in 2025), tea (US$1.51 billion), coconut products (US$1.23 billion), rubber products (US$946 million), food and beverages (US$584 million), spices and essential oils (US$450 million), electrical and electronic components (US$438 million), gems and jewellery and seafood. In services, logistics brought in US$1.85 billion and IT and business process services US$1.64 billion.
- What is Sri Lanka's most famous export? Tea, sold as Ceylon tea, which earned US$1.51 billion in 2025. By value apparel and textiles earn more, at US$4.91 billion. Sri Lanka is also known for Ceylon cinnamon, blue sapphires and coconut products.
- How much did Sri Lanka export in 2025? US$17.25 billion of goods and services, up 5.6% on 2024. Goods were US$13.58 billion, up 6.32%, and services US$3.67 billion, up 2.79%, according to the Export Development Board.
- What is Sri Lanka's export income in 2026? From January to September 2026 Sri Lanka earned US$13.61 billion from exports, up 5.04% on the same months of 2025. Goods were US$10.76 billion, up 5.35%, and services an estimated US$2.85 billion, up 3.88%.
- Which countries buy the most from Sri Lanka? The United States, at US$3.0 billion in 2025 and about a fifth of goods exports, then India (US$1.04 billion), the United Kingdom (US$929 million), Germany, Italy and the Netherlands. In January to September 2026 China, the UAE and Türkiye each took more than US$200 million, and Türkiye grew fastest, up 94%.
- Which Sri Lankan exports are growing fastest? In January to September 2026: electrical and electronic components, up 61.05%, spices and essential oils, up 30.53%, and food and beverages, up 20.90%. Within those, pepper rose 61%, insulated cables 83% and processed food 34%.

## Source products from Sri Lanka
- [Source from Sri Lanka: exporters, products and how to buy](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/): Sri Lanka exported US$13.58 billion of goods in 2025. The largest categories are apparel, tea, coconut products, rubber products, food and beverages, spices and electrical components, and the fastest growing in 2026 are electrical and electronic components, up 61% in the first nine months, and spices, up 30.5%. Buyers in the US, India, the UK and the EU source Ceylon tea and cinnamon, coconut and coir products, industrial tyres and gloves, apparel and a widening range of electrical goods. We match buyers with Sri Lankan exporters who make what they need and check them before we introduce them.
- [Sri Lanka export statistics: 2025 and 2026, by product and by country](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/sri-lanka-export-statistics/): Sri Lanka exported US$17.25 billion of goods and services in 2025, up 5.6%: US$13.58 billion of goods and US$3.67 billion of services. From January to September 2026 exports reached US$13.61 billion, up 5.04%, with goods at US$10.76 billion, up 5.35%. The largest export is apparel and textiles, at US$4.91 billion in 2025, followed by tea, coconut products and rubber products. The fastest growing in 2026 are electrical and electronic components, up 61%, and spices and essential oils, up 30.5%. The United States is the largest market, at about a fifth of goods exports, followed by India and the United Kingdom. CSV: https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/data/sri-lanka-exports-2025-2026.csv
- [Apparel manufacturers in Sri Lanka: activewear, intimates, swimwear and workwear](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/apparel-manufacturing/): Apparel is Sri Lanka's largest export, at US$4.91 billion for apparel and textiles in 2025. Manufacturers make sportswear and activewear, lingerie and intimate wear, swimwear, loungewear, bridal wear, workwear and children's wear, mostly for the US, the EU and the UK. The industry sells on ethical and green manufacturing: 17 factories are LEED certified, and Garments Without Guilt certifies labour standards. Exports are down 5.68% in the first nine months of 2026 as US and EU demand softened, so some factories may have spare capacity.
- [Ceylon tea suppliers and exporters in Sri Lanka: bulk, packets and private label](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/ceylon-tea/): Sri Lanka exported US$1.51 billion of tea in 2025, about 257 million kilograms, and supplied 13% of the world's tea exports in 2024. Ceylon tea is grown in seven regions and graded by elevation, and about 93% is made by orthodox methods. Most tea is sold through the Colombo Tea Auction, which runs every Tuesday and Wednesday. Exporters supply bulk tea, packets, tea bags, green, white and instant tea, and 59% of exports in 2025 were value added. Only 100% Ceylon tea packed in Sri Lanka may carry the Sri Lanka Tea Board's Lion logo.
- [Ceylon cinnamon suppliers and exporters in Sri Lanka: Alba quills, powder and oils](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/ceylon-cinnamon/): Sri Lanka is the world's largest producer and exporter of true cinnamon, Cinnamomum zeylanicum, and Ceylon cinnamon has been a protected geographical indication in the EU since February 2022. Cinnamon exports reached US$221.56 million in the first nine months of 2026, up 31%. Quills are graded by diameter into Alba, Continental, Mexican and Hamburg, and every export of quills, chips and powder must meet the national standard SLS 81:2010 with a clearance certificate. The largest markets are Mexico, the US and Peru.
- [Desiccated coconut, coconut milk and virgin coconut oil suppliers in Sri Lanka](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/coconut-products/): Sri Lanka's coconut and coconut based exports rose 42.66% to US$1.23 billion in 2025, led by coconut cream, coconut oil and milk powder. The Export Development Board ranks Sri Lanka the fourth largest exporter of coconut products, and in 2024 it exported US$138 million of liquid coconut milk and US$112 million of desiccated coconut. Kernel processors hold ISO 22000, FSSC 22000, HACCP and BRC certificates, and every desiccated coconut shipment carries a Coconut Development Authority certificate. Nut supply has been falling, so build price review clauses into contracts.
- [Coco peat and coir suppliers in Sri Lanka: blocks, grow bags, fibre and husk chips](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/coco-peat-coir/): Sri Lanka exported US$197.54 million of coco peat, fibre pith and moulded products in 2024, and the Export Development Board describes it as the third largest coco peat exporter and the largest supplier of brown coir fibre, at about 100,000 tonnes a year. Exporters supply blocks and bricks, grow bags, discs, cubes and plugs, washed, unwashed or buffered with calcium nitrate, plus coir fibre, twine, geotextiles, mats and husk chips. Many products for Europe need RHP certification.
- [Coconut shell activated carbon manufacturers in Sri Lanka](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/activated-carbon/): Sri Lanka is among the top three producers of activated carbon in the world, according to the Export Development Board, and exports reached US$155.55 million in 2024. Exports rose 37.79% in the first nine months of 2026. Producers make granular, powdered and pelletised coconut shell activated carbon for water treatment, air and gas treatment, gold recovery, food and beverage and energy storage, and the main markets are the US, the EU, Japan and South Korea. Grade specifications are agreed supplier by supplier, so ask for a certificate of analysis per lot.
- [Solid tyre manufacturers in Sri Lanka: forklift, industrial and OTR tyres](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/industrial-tyres/): Sri Lanka is the world's leading solid tyre exporter, with about 25% of world demand by the Export Development Board's estimate. Tyres and tubes earned US$522 million in 2025, the largest rubber product line, and solid tyres make up 61% of tyre export value. Manufacturers, including joint ventures with international tyre makers, also produce pneumatic and semi pneumatic tyres, tubes and retreading material. Solid tyres go mainly to the US and the EU; most pneumatic tyre exports go to Asia Pacific.
- [Rubber glove manufacturers in Sri Lanka: examination, surgical, industrial and household gloves](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/rubber-gloves/): Sri Lanka exported US$293 million of industrial and surgical rubber gloves in 2025, its second largest rubber product line after tyres, and glove exports rose 7.58% in the first nine months of 2026. Manufacturers make gloves for healthcare, industrial, household and agricultural use, as well as seals, gaskets, washers, mats, rubber bands and hoses, using Sri Lankan natural rubber including latex crepe. About 75 rubber product exporters are registered with the Board of Investment. For medical gloves in the UK or EU, ask for EN 455 test reports.
- [Electrical cable, transformer and switchgear manufacturers in Sri Lanka](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/electrical-cables-transformers/): Sri Lanka's electrical and electronic component exports reached US$508.86 million in the first nine months of 2026, up 61% and already above the US$438.49 million earned in all of 2025. The Export Development Board credits insulated wires and cables (+82.59%), transformers (+33.46%), switches, boards and panels (+31.49%), telephone and audio equipment (+234.82%) and boilers, engines and pumps (+508.71%). More than 100 manufacturers and service providers work across electronics manufacturing services, components, own products and design, and a Sri Lankan transformer maker has won national utility tenders abroad for 1,040 units in 2014 and 1,000 units in 2017.
- [Sri Lankan spice exporters: black pepper, cloves, nutmeg, essential oils and oleoresins](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/spices-essential-oils/): Sri Lanka exported US$449.9 million of spices, essential oils and oleoresins in 2025, and the sector grew 30.53% in the first nine months of 2026, with pepper up 61% to US$136.26 million. Beyond cinnamon, exporters supply black pepper, cloves, nutmeg and mace, cardamom, ginger and turmeric, essential oils from four main distilleries, 12 smaller distilleries and about 170 field units, and oleoresins. Pepper, cloves, nutmeg and cardamom are sold under the Ceylon Spices geographical indication. Most spices ship in bulk, unprocessed form.
- [Processed food and beverage exporters in Sri Lanka: biscuits, sauces, drinks and feed](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/processed-food-beverages/): Sri Lanka's food and beverage exports rose 24.23% to US$583.89 million in 2025, and processed food rose another 34.19% to US$243.28 million in the first nine months of 2026, with non alcoholic beverages up 46.78%. The Export Development Board lists more than 110 food and beverage manufacturers and marketers making biscuits and wafers, confectionery, sauces, jams, cordials, ready to drink beverages, ready to serve food and animal feed. Most processed food exporters hold ISO 22000, HACCP, BRC, kosher or organic certificates.
- [Seafood exporters in Sri Lanka: yellowfin tuna, swordfish, shrimp and crab](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/seafood/): Sri Lanka exported US$240.19 million of seafood in 2025, led by yellowfin tuna and swordfish, fresh, chilled and frozen, with shrimp, crab, lobster and sea cucumber. The EU lifted its ban on Sri Lankan fishery exports in June 2016, and the Export Development Board counts 55 EU approved processing plants. The largest markets in 2024 were the US, Germany, the UK, France, Italy and the Netherlands. Supply follows the monsoon and yellowfin is under an Indian Ocean catch limit, so agree volumes and a season plan with your supplier.
- [Ceylon sapphires and gems from Sri Lanka: wholesale buying guide](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/gems-jewellery/): Sri Lanka exported US$334 million of gems, diamonds and jewellery in 2025: US$189 million of gemstones, US$127 million of diamonds and US$17.8 million of jewellery, according to the Export Development Board. It is known for Ceylon blue sapphire, padparadscha, star and fancy sapphires and spinel, mined mainly around Ratnapura and Elahera. Only cut and polished stones may be exported, every exporter needs a National Gem and Jewellery Authority licence, and about 70% of the stones exported are foreign in origin, so ask for a lab report that states origin and treatment.
- [Pump, engine and light engineering manufacturers in Sri Lanka](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/light-engineering/): Sri Lanka's exports of boilers, piston engines, pumps and vacuum pumps reached US$171.39 million in the first half of 2026 and grew 508.71% in the first nine months. The wider light engineering industry has more than 500 manufacturing units making pumps, agricultural, tea and rubber processing machinery, castings, aluminium extrusions, fasteners, steel structures and auto parts. The Export Development Board says Sri Lankan makers can serve small order and niche requirements. The Export Development Board reports pumps and engines together with electrical and electronic components, and the growth is from a low base, so check supplier depth case by case.
- [Boat builders in Sri Lanka: fibreglass boats, catamarans, workboats and patrol craft](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/boat-building/): Sri Lankan boatyards build yachts and leisure boats, catamarans, fishing vessels, passenger and crew boats, landing craft, tugs, patrol and rescue craft and pontoons, mostly in fibreglass and composite, with larger vessels in aluminium and steel. Norway bought US$43.1 million of Sri Lankan built boats in 2025, up from US$21 million in 2023. Yards build to Lloyd's Register, DNV, Bureau Veritas and ABS rules, but the Export Development Board names certification as the sector's biggest barrier for leisure boats, so confirm CE or class documents per yard and model.
- [Fruit and vegetable exporters in Sri Lanka: pineapple, banana, papaya and king coconut](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/fruits-vegetables/): Sri Lanka exported US$71.51 million of fruits, nuts and vegetables in 2024, led by vegetables (US$29.79 million) and bananas (US$16.57 million), alongside papaya, gherkins and bottled king coconut water, a fruit indigenous to Sri Lanka. About 65% of fresh produce goes to the Middle East and the Maldives, and almost all processed products go to Europe. Fresh shipments travel with a phytosanitary certificate from the National Plant Quarantine Service, and some farms are GlobalG.A.P. certified. It is a small category, so steady volumes of one fresh line may need several growers.
- [Cut foliage, live plant and aquarium plant exporters in Sri Lanka](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/floriculture/): Sri Lanka exported US$13.67 million of cut flowers and foliage in 2024, mostly foliage such as dracaena and cordyline (US$11.69 million). Exporters also supply aquarium plants including Cryptocoryne, Anubias and Echinodorus. Europe takes 60% of floriculture exports, led by the Netherlands. The main exporters grow in their own nurseries and hold GLOBALG.A.P., MPS and Fair Trade certificates. Units are small, so large programmes may need several growers.
- [Ornamental fish exporters in Sri Lanka: aquarium fish wholesale](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/ornamental-fish/): Sri Lanka exports ornamental fish to more than 68 countries through about 85 active exporters, according to the Export Development Board. Freshwater fish led by guppies are bred on farms all year, while marine fish and invertebrates are mostly collected by divers. The US took about 41% of the US$24.46 million exported in 2024. Exports fell 7.6% to US$22.6 million in 2025 and are down 26.71% in the first nine months of 2026, so check each exporter's current capacity before you plan volumes.
- [Porcelain tableware and ceramics manufacturers in Sri Lanka](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/ceramics-porcelain/): Sri Lanka exported US$20.76 million of tableware and kitchenware in 2024, mostly porcelain and fine china, along with wall and floor tiles and ornamental ware. The Export Development Board says Sri Lankan tableware conforms to US FDA norms and ASTM standards, with in glaze, on glaze and under glaze decoration, heavy metal free designs and microwave safe gold and platinum. The industry uses local quartz, feldspar, dolomite and china clay and employs more than 20,000 people. Main tableware markets include India, the US and Japan.
- [Printing and packaging companies in Sri Lanka: cartons, labels and book printing](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/printing-packaging/): Sri Lankan printers and packaging makers supply tea cartons, printed paperboard boxes, corrugated cartons, labels and garment tags, paper sacks and recycled kraft paper, and print books, catalogues, stationery and calendars on flexo and offset presses. The industry has more than 50 years of prepress experience, and export revenue was an estimated US$118 million in 2019, the latest sector total on the Export Development Board's pages. Much of the packaging serves Sri Lanka's own tea and apparel exporters. Certificates such as FSC, BRCGS or food contact compliance vary by company.
- [Furniture and wood product manufacturers in Sri Lanka](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/wood-furniture/): Sri Lanka's wood exports are mainly furniture, parquet flooring, brush handles, wooden panels and wooden toys. Manufacturers make office, bedroom and kitchen furniture, often in treated rubberwood from rubber trees no longer tapped for latex. India bought US$17.78 million of Sri Lankan furniture and seats in 2025. For the EU, the deforestation regulation applies to wood products for large and medium operators from 30 December 2026, so ask for traceability and legality evidence with every shipment.
- [Footwear and leather goods manufacturers in Sri Lanka](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/leather-footwear/): Sri Lanka's footwear industry can make 25 to 35 million pairs a year, plus 30 to 35 million pairs of rubber thongs, according to the Export Development Board. It makes leather and canvas shoes, safety shoes, rubber boots and sports shoes, and small leather goods such as wallets, belts and bags. Sri Lanka is the only producer of sole crepe, a natural rubber used for unit soles. The sector is small, at US$46.4 million of exports in 2023, and most leather is imported, so check materials and capacity early.
- [Sri Lanka vein graphite, ilmenite and quartz: mineral suppliers and export rules](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/graphite-minerals/): Sri Lanka is the only country that commercially produces natural crystalline vein graphite, graded above 90% carbon, according to the Export Development Board. It also exports ilmenite, rutile and zircon from the Pulmoddai beach sand deposit, high purity vein quartz and mica. Volumes are small: about 4,000 tonnes of vein graphite in 2019 by US Geological Survey estimates. Raw and semi finished minerals need an export licence from the Geological Survey and Mines Bureau.
- [Ayurvedic and herbal product manufacturers in Sri Lanka: herbal teas, oils and natural cosmetics](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/ayurveda-herbal-products/): Sri Lankan manufacturers make herbal teas such as Ranawara, Gotukola, Moringa and Bael flower, ayurvedic massage oils and balms, herbal soaps and hair care, and natural cosmetics, many using Sri Lankan spice oils. Ayurveda is governed by the Ayurveda Act of 1961 and the Department of Ayurveda, and the National Medicines Regulatory Authority covers some products. It is a small, developing export category and we found no separate official export figures, so check each manufacturer's certificates and how its products are classified in your market.
- [How to import from Sri Lanka](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/how-to-import-from-sri-lanka/): Importing from Sri Lanka means agreeing the specification and terms with an exporter, shipping from the Port of Colombo or by air, and using a certificate of origin to claim lower duties where your country offers them. The EU removes duties on 66% of tariff lines under GSP+, the UK gives zero duty on more than 7,000 product lines, and India admits most Sri Lankan goods duty free. Most US imports from Sri Lanka pay a 10% Section 301 tariff on top of normal duties since July 2026. Colombo handled a record 8.29 million TEUs in 2025.
- [Request a quote from Sri Lankan exporters](https://techdestinationsrilanka.lk/source/request-a-quote/)
